quests.hint: Pause after 'here' and after 'minutes'; peak on HALF.
quests.explanation: A confident opening uses short, clear groups and puts the big claim at the end, so 'in half' lands with weight.
quests.textToSpeak: Thank you all for being here. Over the next twenty minutes, I'll show you how we cut onboarding time in half.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and pause where they pause.

quests.explanation: Signposting helps the audience follow the structure. Contrasting PROB-lem with DID makes the difference between the two slides clear.
quests.textToSpeak: The first slide shows the problem; the second shows what we did about it.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and copy which words stand out.

quests.explanation: A three-item summary rises twice and lands on a fall, which tells the audience it is complete.
quests.textToSpeak: So, to summarise: faster onboarding, lower costs, and happier customers.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and match the rise and fall of the voice.

quests.hint: Pause after 'career'; peaks on BUILD-ing and JOIN.
quests.explanation: The long relative clause sounds organised when it is separated from the main statement. BUILD-ing and JOIN carry the answer the interviewer wants to hear.
quests.textToSpeak: What I'm most proud of in my career is building a team that people actually want to join.
quests.instruction: Repeat, keeping each thought group together.

quests.hint: Beats on LED, CROSS-func-tion-al, RE-duced, fif-TEEN.
quests.explanation: Achievements are delivered with steady beats and a firm number: fif-TEEN percent lands on a fall.
quests.textToSpeak: In my previous role, I led a cross-functional project that reduced costs by fifteen percent.
quests.instruction: Tap the beats as you listen, then repeat in the same rhythm.

quests.hint: Peaks on DI-rect and FAIR; keep 'I think they'd say I'm' light.
quests.explanation: Modest self-description sounds confident when the contrast words DI-rect and FAIR carry the peaks and the pitch falls at the end.
quests.textToSpeak: If you asked my colleagues, I think they'd say I'm direct but fair.
quests.instruction: Copy the pitch pattern as closely as you can.

quests.explanation: Empathy and action are different messages, so the fall on 'frustrating' shows that you have listened. The peak on RIGHT then shows commitment to a solution.
quests.textToSpeak: I understand this has been frustrating, and I'd like to make it right.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and match the rise and fall of the voice.

quests.explanation: A refusal is easier to accept when it is paired with an offer. CAN and CAN'T are the contrast, so the customer hears what they get and what they do not.
quests.textToSpeak: Let me be clear about what I can do: I can refund the fee, but I can't waive the deposit.
quests.instruction: Repeat, matching the peaks of stress exactly.

quests.hint: Peak on PA-tience and fall on 'out'.
quests.explanation: Thanks for patience should sound sincere, not automatic. A peak on PA-tience and a soft fall on 'out' close the call warmly.
quests.textToSpeak: I completely appreciate your patience while we sort this out.
quests.instruction: Listen for the final pitch movement, then repeat.

quests.explanation: The sentence corrects a diagnosis: the delay is in one area, not another. DE-sign and ap-PRO-vals are the contrast, and stress makes it clear where to act.
quests.textToSpeak: We're not behind on the design; we're behind on the approvals.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the contrast in the speaker's voice.

quests.hint: Beats on PRO-to-type, TEST-ing, MON-day, LAUNCH, TRACK.
quests.explanation: A status update sounds confident when it follows a steady pattern. Each item has a beat, so the listener hears a series of clear milestones rather than a blur.
quests.textToSpeak: Here's where we are: the prototype is done, testing starts Monday, and launch is still on track.
quests.instruction: Keep the small words quick and match the pacing.

quests.explanation: Raising a risk should be clear but calm. Peaks on FLAG-ging and SUP-pli-er show the topic without making it sound alarming.
quests.textToSpeak: One risk worth flagging is that we're depending on a single supplier.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and match the rise and fall of the voice.

quests.explanation: A conditional offer rises on the concession, THOU-sand, and falls on the condition, YEARS, showing that the two are tied together.
quests.textToSpeak: We'd be happy to go to twelve thousand, provided the contract runs for two years.
quests.instruction: Listen for the final pitch movement, then repeat.

quests.explanation: A polite counter acknowledges before it pushes back. FAIR shows respect and SCOPE explains why the offer is still not enough.
quests.textToSpeak: That's a fair offer, but it doesn't reflect the scope of the work.
quests.instruction: Repeat, matching the peaks of stress exactly.

quests.explanation: A collaborative question rises on 'middle' to invite a reply, and 'what would work on your side' closes with a fall.
quests.textToSpeak: Perhaps we could meet in the middle; what would work on your side?
quests.instruction: Repeat, matching where the voice rises and where it falls.

quests.explanation: The sentence has a cause and an effect, so the pause after 'late' helps the listener separate them. AL-ways and DAY show why the delay matters.
quests.textToSpeak: The issue is that the data arrives late, so the reports are always a day behind.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the same chunks and pauses.

quests.hint: Beats on UP-loads, CHECKS, RUN, HANGS.
quests.explanation: Describing a process is easier to follow when each step has a beat. UP-loads, CHECKS, RUN and HANGS give the listener a clear sequence, and the final beat lands on the problem.
quests.textToSpeak: What happens is the file uploads, the checks run, and then it just hangs.
quests.instruction: Repeat with the same bounce and timing as the model.

quests.explanation: The first half says what you tried and the second says what happened. The rise on 'twice' tells the listener that bad news is coming.
quests.textToSpeak: We've tried restarting it twice, but the error keeps coming back.
quests.instruction: Listen for the final pitch movement, then repeat.

quests.explanation: 'Based on what we've seen' gives the reason, so it is quick. The peak on SEC-ond then names the recommendation, which is what the listener wants.
quests.textToSpeak: Based on what we've seen, I'd recommend the second option.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the contrast in the speaker's voice.

quests.explanation: Advice with steps is easier to follow when each step is a separate group. The pauses after 'small' and 'results' show the order and make the plan sound achievable.
quests.textToSpeak: My advice would be to start small, measure the results, and then scale up.
quests.instruction: Follow the speaker's phrasing as you repeat.

quests.explanation: 'I'd lean towards' is a hedge, so it sounds like an opinion, not an order. CLOUD and main-TAIN carry the reasons, so the listener remembers why.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd lean towards the cloud option, mainly because it's easier to maintain.
quests.instruction: Repeat, matching where the voice rises and where it falls.

quests.explanation: A formal request rises on 'agreed' to keep it polite, and SUM-ma-ry is the key noun.
quests.textToSpeak: Would it be possible to get a written summary of what we've agreed?
quests.instruction: Listen for the final pitch movement, then repeat.

quests.explanation: Polite deadlines sound gentle when the request is emphasised more than the deadline. The stress on ap-PRE-ci-ate makes it sound like a favour, and the rise on 'Thursday' keeps it open.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd really appreciate it if you could confirm by Thursday.
quests.instruction: Follow the speaker's pitch up and down as you repeat.

quests.explanation: 'Could you kindly' is very polite, so the rise on 'problem' invites an honest answer. It sounds like you want to help, not that you are testing them.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you kindly let me know if that timeframe would be a problem?
quests.instruction: Listen once, then repeat with the same melody.

quests.explanation: Blaming yourself for unclear wording avoids blaming the listener. The fall on 'well' takes responsibility, and OP-tion-al makes the corrected point clear.
quests.textToSpeak: Sorry, I don't think I explained that well; what I meant to say was that the fee is optional.
quests.instruction: Follow the speaker's pitch up and down as you repeat.

quests.explanation: 'At cross purposes' says both people are right in different ways. BUD-get and TIME-line are the two topics, so stress shows exactly where the confusion happened.
quests.textToSpeak: I think we may be talking at cross purposes; I was referring to the budget, not the timeline.
quests.instruction: Copy the emphasis so the meaning stays the same.

quests.explanation: Paraphrasing what you heard lets the other person correct you. The rise on 'correctly' asks for confirmation, and the fall on 'shipping' states the detail you understood.
quests.textToSpeak: If I've understood you correctly, you'd like us to cover the cost of the return shipping.
quests.instruction: Copy the pitch pattern as closely as you can.

quests.hint: Peaks on PLEAS-ure and CON-ver-SA-tion; rise on 'sometime'.
quests.explanation: A friendly goodbye needs warmth, not formality. PLEAS-ure and CON-ver-SA-tion carry the feeling, and the rise on 'sometime' makes the invitation open.
quests.textToSpeak: It's been a pleasure meeting you; I'd love to continue the conversation over coffee sometime.
quests.instruction: Follow the speaker closely and copy every part of the delivery.

quests.hint: Chunks: 'I work in logistics' / 'mostly on the operations side' / 'so I'm always keen to hear' / 'how other people approach it'.
quests.explanation: Introduce yourself in chunks so each part is easy to process, with the peaks on LO-gis-tics and OP-er-A-tions.
quests.textToSpeak: I work in logistics, mostly on the operations side, so I'm always keen to hear how other people approach it.
quests.instruction: Repeat as naturally as the model, keeping the same shape.

quests.explanation: A formal compliment sounds sincere when the important words get real stress. GREAT and HON-our show respect without sounding scripted.
quests.textToSpeak: Thank you for the introduction; I've heard great things about your work, and it's a real honour to meet you.
quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then reproduce the phrase with the same feeling.
